title: Sudarshan Yadav v. State of U.P. and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Sadhna Rani (Thakur), J.
disposition: Writ disposed; objections reconsidered under Clause 8.1(b); recovery stayed.
headnote: Where written objections to a provisional assessment had not been decided, the Allahabad High Court disposed of the writ by directing the assessing officer to fix a personal hearing, consider every objection afresh by a reasoned speaking order strictly under Clause 8.1(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and withhold coercive recovery on the 7 July 2020 demand until that fresh decision or two months, whichever is earlier.
facts: Sudarshan Yadav challenged a 7 July 2020 demand following a 12 December 2019 inspection alleging theft. He said his father Rampyarey Yadav held a valid domestic connection, the theft allegations were false, and his 21 January 2020 objections to the 29 December 2019 provisional assessment were never decided: no personal hearing was fixed before the final assessment. Licensee's counsel submitted that, once the provisional notice was served, personal hearing was unnecessary unless demanded.

holding_units.topic: consideration of objections to provisional assessment
holding_units.holding: Objections to a provisional assessment, including those going to the inspection report, must be considered afresh strictly in accordance with Clause 8.1(b). The assessing officer was directed to fix a personal hearing on the consumer's 21 January 2020 objections, deal with every point in a reasoned speaking order on the 29 December 2019 provisional assessment, and take no coercive steps on the 7 July 2020 demand until that fresh decision or two months. If the consumer fails to appear on the date fixed, the licensee may proceed in accordance with law.

principle_tags.application: Coercive recovery on the 7 July 2020 demand was stayed until a fresh Clause 8.1(b) decision (or two months), so the existing demand could not be enforced while objections to the provisional assessment remained to be decided.

not_decided.point: Whether the 12 December 2019 inspection established theft, and whether the 7 July 2020 demand was valid on merits
not_decided.note: The Court remanded for fresh consideration under Clause 8.1(b) without deciding the theft allegations or the quantum of the demand.

not_decided.point: Whether Clause 8.1(b) requires a personal hearing unless the consumer demands one
not_decided.note: The licensee argued that personal hearing is not required unless demanded. The Court said “Be that as it may” and directed a hearing as a further opportunity, without deciding that contention.
